    • Taskmaster kicks Romanoff's gun out of her hands and the two engage in hand-to-hand combat, and Taskmaster takes Romanoff down. The two flip to their feet simultaneously and study each other.[32]
    • Taskmaster is ordered to redirect her attention to her primary target, so she turns, heading for the package. Romanoff realizes that she is not there for her. Romanoff engages Taskmaster, who pins her down and picks her up by her hair before sending her flying back. Romanoff gets back up, but Taskmaster kicks her back again.[32]
    • Taskmaster walks toward the package, so Romanoff uses a grappling hook to attach to Taskmaster and a support beam, sending Taskmaster flying back. Taskmaster cuts part of the rope while Romanoff retrieves the package, and Taskmaster swings on the rope to Romanoff and attacks her with a sword.[32]
    • Romanoff uses Taskmaster's shield to defend herself as the pair fight over the package, which Taskmaster gets. Taskmaster kicks Romanoff off of the bridge, sending her flying into the river. Taskmaster sees that the package is empty and looks over the bridge for Romanoff.[32]
  • Romanoff surfaces before laying down and taking the vials of Red Dust out of her pocket. Among the vials she finds a set of photo booth pictures of her and Yelena Belova. Romanoff swears under her breath and leaves for Budapest.[32]
  • After spending the remainder of Friday and some of Saturday in Germany, Peter Parker flies home with Tony Stark and Happy Hogan.[153]

26th

  • Peter Parker is returned home to Queens by Tony Stark in the early hours. He and Stark film an alibi video for where Stark had taken him for the weekend, to give to May Parker.[153]
  • Parker is delighted when Stark says he can keep his new suit, and then Stark and Hogan drive off, leaving Parker with his case to return to his normal life.[153][181]
  • Tony Stark arrives back at the Avengers Compound.[130]
  • Peter Parker tells his aunt May Parker of how he got into another fight, covering up for his secret identity as Spider-Man, and his aunt goes along with his story, despite suspecting he is not telling the truth.[130]
  • Peter Parker discovers a portable holographic computer that Stark has programmed into his new Web-Shooters.[130]

27th

  • Natasha Romanoff arrives in Budapest and gets off the train.[32]
  • Romanoff arrives at her former safe house, and looks for Yelena Belova. She ascends in the elevator and sighs.[32]
  • She gets out of the elevator and retrieves a hidden gun, beginning to pick the lock. Belova announces herself, and Romanoff says that she is aware that Belova knows that she is there. Romanoff reveals that she is unsure of whether she can trust Belova, and Belova says that she feels the same way about Romanoff.[32]
  • Romanoff asks if they were going to talk like adults, and they find each other, holding guns on each other. They threaten each other as they walk through the safe house, and steal each other's guns in unison. They begin fighting each other without the guns, pushing each other against walls.[32]
  • Romanoff pins Belova to the counter tells her to stay down, but Belova breaks a plate over Romanoff's head, forcing her to back up. Belova attacks Romanoff with a towel, but Romanoff wraps it around Belova's neck. Belova falls and kicks Romanoff, causing her to fly backwards. The two right themselves and Belova grabs a knife while Romanoff grabs a three-hole-punch.[32]
  • The pair resume fighting as Romanoff gets the knife out of Belova's hand and they lock each other in place. Belova pushes Romanoff against a wall, and Romanoff grabs a curtain and wraps it around Belova's neck. Belova wraps the other end of the curtain around Romanoff's neck and the pair flip each other to the ground. They begin choking each other, but declare a truce and release each other. They grasp for air and Romanoff comments that Belova grew up.[32]
  • Belova gets drinks while Romanoff asks about Belova going to Budapest. Belova explains that she came because she assumed that Romanoff would not. Belova asks about the holes in the walls, and Romanoff says that they were made by arrows. Romanoff asks why she would send the Red Dust if Belova did not think she would come, and Belova yells at her for bringing it to Budapest.[32]
  • Belova explains that the dust is able to free people from chemical mind control, and Belova asks why she did not take the dust to Tony Stark, and Romanoff says that they are not on speaking terms. Belova complains about the timing, and Romanoff scolds Belova for putting her in danger. Belova says that she sent the dust to her because she is a superhero.[32]
  • Belova says that she continually checked the news for a headline about the Avengers taking down the Red Room, surprising Romanoff, who believed that the Red Room had been gone for years. Belova expresses shock that Romanoff believes Dreykov. At Belova's request, Romanoff explains how she and Clint Barton killed him. Belova asks if Romanoff confirmed the kill, but Romanoff says that there was no body to check. Belova says that Romanoff is forgetting Dreykov's daughter, giving Romanoff pause.[32]
  • Chase for the Red Dust:
    • The roof of the safe house explodes as Belova and Romanoff take cover. Several Black Widows enter while Belova puts the Red Dust in her backpack. Belova rushes to Romanoff and triggers the lights to explode, giving the pair the opportunity they need to momentarily incapacitate the Widows and escape.[32]
    • The pair rush outside to find more Widows, who begin firing at them. Belova throws a grenade at two of the Widows and runs along with Romanoff, telling her that there is a motorcycle they can use if they can get to it. Ingrid chases after them, as they push a chimney over while holding it.[32]
    • Ingrid grabs onto Romanoff as chimney slowly falls, and Romanoff holds onto her, trying to keep Ingrid alive. Ingrid slices at Romanoff, causing her to let go, and falls into the alley below. The chimney crashes into a building, sending Belova through a window but causing Romanoff to fall and hit several vents.[32]
    • Romanoff approaches Ingrid and offers to help. Ingrid instead points her Black Widow's Bite at her, Dreykov then orders Ingrid to kill herself. Ingrid tells Romanoff that she does not want to do it before firing at herself, resulting in her death.[32]
    • Romanoff approaches Ingrid as Belova reaches the bottom of the stairs, ready to give her the Red Dust, but sees that Ingrid is dead. Belova asks if Romanoff believes her about Dreykov being alive, and Romanoff asks how many other Widows there are. Belova says that there are enough and the pair rush into a nearby building, leaving Ingrid's body behind.[32]
    • Belova and Romanoff rush to the motorcycle. Belova asks where the keys are, and Romanoff reveals that she has them. They get on the motorcycle as they are approached by a tank driven by Taskmaster, who chases them through the street.[32]
    • Belova and Romanoff turn into an alley while Taskmaster drives forward, and the girls come out on the other side, pursued by a widow. They ride down the stairs and crash into a stone rail, sending them flying over it into the street nearby[32]
    • A man gets out of his car as Belova points her gun at him, causing him to flee. Romanoff scolds her for stealing the car, and Belova sarcastically suggests chasing him down and returning it while Romanoff gets in the driver's seat.[32]
    • The Widow resumes her chase, catching up to them on the street, before she begins firing at them. Romanoff begins driving as the Widow follows on her motorcycle.[32]
    • Romanoff turns into a plaza, Belova remarks that there is now no way out, Romanoff replies that the gate was not there eight years prior.[177]
    • Belova looks back as the Widow fires at them. She asks Romanoff if there is a plan, and Romanoff says that the plan was to drive away. Belova says that it is a bad plan and grabs the wheel, turning the car around. While Romanoff drives backwards, Belova kicks the passenger door open, hitting a street sign, causing it to fly backward and hit the Widow's motorcycle, knocking her off of it.[32]
    • Romanoff continues to drive as Taskmaster begins following them again, while preparing a bow and quiver. Taskmaster fires an explosive arrow under Romanoff's car, flipping it and sending it into a train station.[32]
    • Romanoff and Belova get out of the car as Taskmaster follows them into the station, they slide down the handrail on the escalator. Taskmaster throws her shield at the pair, who dodge it, causing it to lodge itself in a support beam. Belova and Romanoff run and hide in the vent. Taskmaster follows Belova's blood and goes below ground, while Romanoff and Belova hide in the vent and watch.[32]
  • Belova makes herself a tourniquet as Romanoff explains that she and Barton spent two days hiding in the vents, before asking who Taskmaster is. Belova explains that she can mimic anyone she's seen and is only deployed for high priority projects. Romanoff insists that Dreykov being alive does not make sense, and Belova again asks about Dreykov's daughter. Romanoff explains that she needed the young girl to lead her to Dreykov so that she could kill him. Romanoff explains that she needed out.[32]
  • Romanoff and Belova go to Varoil Üzemanyag, where Romanoff asks where the Red Room is, and Belova explains that the place is too secure for her to know. Romanoff says that she is struggling to believe that the Red Room stayed off her radar, and Belova explains that if she were killed, one of the bigger Avengers would go after him.[32]
  • Belova asks where Romanoff thought she was, and Romanoff explains that she thought Belova was living a normal life and that she did not think Belova wanted to see her. Belova suggested that Romanoff did not want her younger sister tagging along, and Romanoff says that Belova is not her sister. Belova countered that the Avengers were not really her family.[32]
  • Belova asks why Romanoff always poses while fighting, making fun of her. Romanoff says that she does not pose, and Romanoff says that she was trying to do something good to make up for the pain she caused and trying to be more than a killer. Belova said that they are still trained killers, commenting that young girls call Romanoff their hero despite her being a killer.[32]
  • Romanoff and Belova find a table as Belova treats her wound. Belova explains that the Red Dust was synthesized in secret by an older Widow, and that she was cured on a mission to retrieve it. Belova explains the difference between the brainwashing Romanoff experienced and the chemical subjugation she experienced, and that she is still not sure what part of her is herself.[32]
  • Romanoff treats Belova's wound as Belova explains that the Red Dust they have is all that is left, and that he continues taking children every day and kills the ones who do not survive training. Belova says that thanks to Romanoff and Alexei Shostakov's efforts, no one is looking for Dreykov. Romanoff expresses surprise that Belova mentioned Shostakov.[32]
  • Belova and Romanoff look at a nearby family, causing Belova to ask if Romanoff had looked for her biological parents. Romanoff says that her mom abandoned her. Belova explains the pretend backstory she gave to herself, asking asking about Romanoff's, who says that she never lets herself be alone long enough to think about it.[32]
  • Belova asks if Romanoff ever wanted children, and says that she wants a dog. Romanoff asks where Belova is going to go, and Belova says that she does not have anywhere to go back to. Belova realizes that Romanoff wants to inspire her to help kill Dreykov, and says that it sounds like a lot of work. Romanoff suggests that it could be fun, and Belova agrees. Romanoff says that she remembers where the father of the family they saw put the keys to the car,so she and Belova clink their bottles and steal the car.[32]
  • While driving, Belova tells Romanoff that her vest is the first piece of clothing she ever bought for herself, talking about how the pockets are useful and how she made her own modifications. Belova explains that she wants to do things with her newfound control, and Romanoff says that she likes the vest, pleasing Belova. Romanoff suggests that she knows who would know the Red Room's location, saying that they will need a jet.[32]
  • Peter Parker is putting on his Spider-Man Suit when he hears May Parker telling him to go to bed so he is not groggy in the morning. Peter tells her he will finish his homework then do so. Spider-Man then goes out the window and starts surveying the city, eventually falling asleep on a roof.[182][183]

28th

  • Spider-Man wakes up to the sound of sirens and looks around. When he goes to capture the Enforcers, a crow comes out of nowhere and grabs his mask off of his head. Peter starts getting worried as he cannot stop crime with his identity exposed. He eventually finds a clothesline and grabs a shirt, wrapping it around his head to use as a mask.[182][183]
  • He then gets to the Enforcers and jokes around with them, annoying Fancy Dan and Ox. Spider-Man then webs them up and lets the police finish the work. A police officer mistakes him as "shirt-man". Peter then returns to his room where May Parker walks in, expecting him to be asleep. Peter is wide awake and joins her for breakfast.[182][183]
  • Natasha Romanoff and Yelena Belova meet Rick Mason, upset that he has provided a helicopter instead of a jet. Mason explains that he did not have time as Romanoff and Belova inspect the helicopter.[32]
  • Mason tells Romanoff that he was contacted by Thaddeus Ross to the point where he had contacts declining his calls. Romanoff continues making fun of Mason, who calls her annoying. Romanoff says that she will make it up to him and enters the helicopter. Mason expresses his doubt and closes the door.[32]
  • Daisy Johnson awakes from a dream where she and Phil Coulson are trapped in a Containment Module on a desolate planet, desperately hoping to escape.[180]
  • Jemma Simmons approaches Johnson in the Containment Module, in order to obtain more information about Hive and his plans.[180]
  • Melinda May uses the Quinjet with Alphonso Mackenzie, Lincoln Campbell, and Elena Rodriguez on board to successfully travel underwater and infiltrate the missile silo.[180]
  • Battle at the Pacific Missile Silo:
    • The team infiltrate Hive's location and, using the nuclear codes that Glenn Talbot obtained from General Andaz, they stop the missile's launch.[180]
    • Hive swears to show S.H.I.E.L.D. his rage as he commands Holden Radcliffe to take two Primitives with him to reset the launch. Hive is lured by Campbell into Mackenzie's trap: a giant Theta Brain-Wave Frequency Machine to pull forward all the different personalities in that the dark Inhuman has absorbed over the millennia. Hive, trying to get his mind under control, orders Giyera and Hellfire to disconnect the warhead, since there is no hope of launching the missile now. May, seeking the warhead, frees Radcliffe from the Primitives, while Rodriguez frees the hostages from the conquered missile silo. However, R. Giyera takes the warhead and flees.[180]
    • When the team attempt to escape, they are confronted by Hive; however, they capture him in a Containment Module full of Suspension Gel.[180]
  • In Seventh Circle Prison, Alexei Shostakov wins an arm wrestling match and tells a story about fighting Captain America. He wins another arm wrestling match and continues his story while he is given a new tattoo.[32]
  • Ursa Major sits across from Shostakov and prepares to arm wrestle him while asking what year he fought Captain America in. Shostakov says it was in the 1980s. Ursa Major mentions that Captain America was still frozen, so Shostakov asks if Ursa Major is calling him a liar. Shostakov slams Ursa Major's hand against the table, breaking his wrist. Shostakov laughs at Ursa Major while he receives a mail call.[32]
  • Shostakov goes to receive his mail, and the prison guards and brag about having stolen the food mailed to him. He is given the rest of the his mail.[32]
  • Escape from the Seventh Circle Prison:
    • Shostakov sits down and sees that he was mailed a doll of himself. He picks it up and pulls the string, causing the head to pop off and reveal an earpiece. He puts it in and hears Romanoff telling him that it is his lucky day. Looking at Belova's map, Romanoff tells Shostakov to move near the south wall of the prison.[32]
    • Shostakov approaches the window and grabs the guard through the glass, pulling him through. He pulls another guard against a metal bar.[32]
    • Romanoff and Belova approach the prison and give him instructions, telling him not to make a scene. Shostakov begins running, and an inmate shouts that Shostakov is escaping. Shostakov begins fighting the riot guards that approach him, and Romanoff realizes that Shostakov made a scene. Shostakov kicks down the exterior door and runs through the outside, asking Romanoff what to do next. Romanoff explains that she and Belova will get him out, and Shostakov notices their helicopter above the prison.[32]
    • Shostakov notices prisoners running at him and tries to escape, while guards run on the upper level and lock down the facility, firing at prisoners. Following Romanoff's instructions, Shostakov jumps to the upper level, but is tased and falls back down.[32]
    • Belova says that Shostakov will never make it, so Romanoff tells Belova to get her closer.[32]
    • Shostakov watches Romanoff jump out of the helicopter and land on the upper level to fight the guards. She lands and poses, which Belova comments on. Romanoff incapacitates several guards, but several more begin firing at the helicopter, forcing Belova to dodge them, nearly cutting Romanoff with the helicopter blades.[32]
    • Shostakov runs through the yard and looks up, during the chaos, he gets into a brief fight with Ursa Major and some other prisoners.[177]
    • Belova apologizes for nearly killing Romanoff, who yells at her to back up. A guard begins firing at Belova, causing her to leave the controls and fire a rocket at the guard, blowing the watchtower up.[32]
    • Belova resumes control and notices that the explosion caused an avalanche, commenting that it would be a cool way to die. Shostakov asks if the avalanche is a good sign, and Romanoff tells him to move.[32]
    • The prisoners cower at the avalanche while Shostakov jumps off of a riot shield and climbs the gates of the yard.[32]
    • Prisoners and guards run into the prison while Romanoff yells at Belova to get them out. Belova maneuvers back towards the prison while Shostakov makes his way to the upper level.[32]
    • Romanoff grabs onto the rope dangling from the helicopter. Shostakov watches the avalanche start to consume the prison, screaming as the helicopter seemingly passes Shostakov. Belova turns and allows Romanoff to grab Shostakov, barely escaping the avalanche in time.[32]
  • Romanoff and Shostakov enter the helicopter as he shouts a farewell to the prison while Romanoff enters the copilot seat. Shostakov expresses pride in the girls before realizing that they cannot hear him. He puts on headphones with a microphone, and Belova punches him in the face.[32]
  • Shostakov asks why Belova is being aggressive, suggesting she is on her period. Belova scolds him, explaining that the Red Room's graduation ceremony removed her uterus, preventing her from getting her period. Belova describes the procedure, upsetting Shostakov.[32]
  • Shostakov thanks them for coming for him, and Romanoff demands to know how to get to the Red Room. Shostakov suggests that she was indoctrinated into the Western agenda, and Romanoff explains that she chose to go west since the Avengers treated her like family. Shostakov expresses doubt, and Romanoff demands to know where the Red Room is.[32]
  • Shostakov confesses to not know where the Red Room is, and explains that his mission in Ohio was boring and upsetting, and complains that he was then put in prison for annoying Dreykov. Shostakov tells them to ask where Melina Vostokoff is, surprising Belova and Romanoff, who believed that Vostokoff was dead.[32]
  • Shostakov explains that Vostokoff was the strategist, and that she worked directly for Dreykov more than he did. Romanoff realizes that Vostokoff still works for the Red Room, and Shostakov says that she works outside of Saint Petersburg. Although Belova insists that they do not have enough fuel, Shostakov insists that they will make it.[32]
  • Thaddeus Ross and his men arrest Rick Mason, after searching his home, they find a note from Romanoff, saying "Come after me."[177]
  • Mackenzie informs Johnson that they have captured Hive.[180]
  • While he is assuring the base is sealed off, Fitz realizes what "Absolution" is: the releasing of the Absolution Virus in the Playground. Hellfire activates the trap, turning several S.H.I.E.L.D. agents into Primitives.[180]
  • Romanoff, Belova, and Shostakov's helicopter crash-lands, having run out of fuel. Shostakov, Belova, and Romanoff leave, and Shostakov says that they should have brought a Quinjet. As the trio walks, Shostakov asks to tell Romanoff something important. Shostakov asks whether Captain America talked about Shostakov.[32]
  • Romanoff scolds Shostakov for focusing on himself, and he asks if he did something wrong. He says that he only ever loved the girls, trying to make sure she would succeed and that everything worked at, talking about Belova's status as an assassin and Romanoff's status as an Avenger. He expresses pride in the girls' high kill counts, hugging them. Romanoff breaks free of Shostakov's hug, and Shostakov turns his attention to Belova, who also leaves.[32]
  • Ross offers Mason a deal; Mason will call Romanoff to get her location, and Ross will not arrest him. Mason agrees, calls Romanoff, and using a coded message, informs her what has happened. Romanoff understands Mason's warnings, and informs Belova and Shostakov.[177]
  • The group begin walking and Belova asks if they are there yet. Shostakov explains that they will know when they are there due to the sound of pigs.[32]
  • Vostokoff experiments with pigs, giving them orders and having them navigate a maze. She rewards the pigs who made it, and receives an alert from a proximity monitor. Vostokoff opens the gate to the maze and orders the pigs to return to their pen where it is safe, and they go.[32]
  • Vostokoff receives her gun and aims it at the hills, using her sight to see that it is Romanoff, Belova, and Shostokov.[32]
  • The three approach Vostokoff, who silently guides them inside her house and welcomes them. Romanoff watches Vostokoff open a weapons cabinet and threatens her, but Vostokoff says that she is putting away her weapon.[32]
  • Belova goes to the dining room table and sits down.[32]
  • Shostakov sits in the bathroom, nervous.[32]
  • Vostokoff leaves her weapons closet while Romanoff asks if there are booby traps. Vostokoff says they did not raise them to fall into traps, and Romanoff counters by saying that she did not raise them at all. Vostokoff says that if Romanoff got soft, it was not on her watch.[32]
  • Belova sits at the table.[32]
  • Shostakov begins struggling to put on his Red Guardian Uniform.[32]
  • Romanoff, Vostokoff, and Belova hear Shostakov struggling from the table, and Vostokoff suggests that they drink and uncaps a bottle.[32]
  • Shostakov struggles to get the shirt of his uniform on.[32]
  • Shostakov finally leaves the bathroom in his full uniform. He says it still fits, and Vostokoff whistles and applauds him. Shostakov sits down and sings to himself, and expresses joy that their family has reunited. Vostokoff suggests no longer using the term "family," and Romanoff agrees.[32]
  • Romanoff attempts to demand information from Vostokoff, but Shostakov interrupts and tells Vostokoff that she is still beautiful, she reponds saying that while he gained weight, he is still attractive. Romanoff cuts them off and again attempts to gain information, but Vostokoff cuts her off and tells her not to slouch. Romanoff says that she is not, and they argue over this, and Shostakov tells Romanoff to listen to her mother.[32]
  • Romanoff again attempts to gain information, but Belova cuts her off and says that she does not want food, and Vostokoff insists that she eat. Romanoff demands to know the location of Red Room Academy, explaining that killing Dreykov is unfinished business, but Vostokoff says that it is impossible, and that they never saw the culmination of their work in Ohio.[32]
  • Vostokoff calls Alexei into the room and rewards him, causing Shostakov to realize that the pig was named after him. Vostokoff comments on his obedience, and gives Alexei the command to stop breathing. Alexei obeys while Vostkoff explains that the North Institute they had infiltrated was a front for Hydra's experiments with chemical subjugation.[32]
  • Alexei passes out, and Vostokoff explains that the science has become so exact that a subject commanded to stop breathing would have to obey. Romanoff tells her that she has made her point, and Vostokoff allows Alexei to breathe again and tells him to return to his pen.[32]
  • Vostokoff says that Dreykov has agents planted around the world, and Belova asks if they know who they test it on. Vostokoff says that she does not know, and Shostakov claims she is lying and that she was Dreykov's architect. The pair begin arguing about who was closer to Dreykov, and Romanoff demands that they shut up, calling Shostakov an idiot and Vostokoff a coward.[32]
  • Romanoff says that their family was never real, upsetting Belova, who insists that it was real to her. She says that no one told her that their family was fake and reveals that she was one of the chemically subjugated agents, asking if Romanoff is going to say anything about how she got out. Vostokoff attempts to comfort Belova, who gets up and leaves with a bottle of alcohol. Romanoff calls after Belova, who refuses and enters another room, closing the door.[32]
  • Vostokoff begins to say that she did not know that Belova was subjugated, and Shostakov comforts her, saying that it is okay and he will talk to her.[32]
  • Shostakov goes to Belova, who says that she does not want to talk. Shostakov agrees to just sit and sits next to her in silence.[32]
  • Vostokoff and Romanoff sit in silence, and Romanoff gets up to kill Dreykov herself. Vostokoff says that she will get herself killed, and Romanoff suggests that she does not care. Romanoff says that Vostokoff was not the first mother to abandon her, but Vostokoff tells her that Romanoff was not abandoned, but selected by a program that tested for genetic potential in infants.[32]
  • Vostokoff explains that her family was paid off, but that her mother never stopped looking until she was killed. Romanoff says that she thought of her mother every day, and Vostokoff says she finds it best not to look into the past. Romanoff asks why she saved the family photo album from Ohio and looks through it, reminiscing about the day they took pictures of fake memories.[32]
  • Romanoff asks Vostokoff why she is working in the Red Room, and Vostokoff explains that she did not have a choice after being brainwashed four times before Romanoff was born. Romanoff says that it is not her fault she was born into the Red Room, and Vostokoff asks how she kept her heart. Romanoff reminds Vostokoff that she used to say that pain makes people stronger, and says that her teachings kept Romanoff alive.[32]
  • Vostokoff apologizes, confessing that she had already alerted the Red Room and that they would be there any minute. They begin mobilizing a plan to take down the Red Room.[32]
  • Preparing weapons, Romanoff reviews the plan, saying that she will activate her tracker once she is inside the Red Room so that Thaddeus Ross will come. Vostokoff points out that she is still a fugitive, and Romanoff simply asks if Vostokoff can land the facility. Vostokoff says that if she is confined on Level 0, she can activate the landing protocol. Vostokoff realizes that she only has one set of earpieces, and Romanoff says that she will give the other one to Belova.[32]
  • Shostakov tells Belova a story about him ice fishing with his father and his father urinating on him to prevent frostbite, despite Belova asking him to stop talking. Belova asks how the story is relevant, and Shostakov says that he was talking about fathers. Belova scolds Shostakov for the way he talked about their time in Ohio as a bad thing, while she viewed him as everything.[32]
  • Vostokoff explains that even if he can get her access to the database, she would not be able to take it due to a pheromonal lock that would prevent them from hurting him. Vostokoff explains that the only workaround is to momentarily sever the nerve from her nose. Romanoff smiles and says that she can handle it.[32]
  • Belova gets upset when she deduces that he does not care and that he only cares about his glory days, referring to him as "Crimson Dynamo." Shostakov corrects her, saying that he went by Red Guardian, and Belova yells at him to leave. He stands up to leave, but stops and begins singing American Pie, Belova's favorite song as a kid. Belova laughs and joins.[32]
  • Ambush at Melina Vostokoff's Homestead:
    • A light suddenly turns on outside as the Red Room surrounds the house. Soldiers approach as Shostakov tells Belova to get down. Shostakov is hit with a dart, which he pulls out easily. He prepares to brag, but he gets hit with several more, knocking him out. Belova checks his pulse and prepares her gun as soldiers surround the house.[32]
    • Belova wanders through the house, gun ready.[32]
    • A helicopter lands with Taskmaster inside.[32]
    • Belova searches through the house and finds Vostokoff, who she believes to be Romanoff, passed out.[32]
    • Taskmaster enters the house.[32]
    • Disguised as Vostokoff, Romanoff stands in front of Belova and apologizes before shooting her.[32]
    • Taskmaster approaches "Vostokoff," who tells her not to keep Dreykov waiting.[32]
  • Battle of the Playground:
    • The Primitives free Hive from captivity. He wants to use the Quinjets' high altitude capabilities to launch the warhead in space, to turn all Humans into primitive Inhumans.[180]
    • After Alphonso Mackenzie leaves, Daisy Johnson escapes from the Containment Module and goes to confront Hive. She begs him to sway her again, but he cannot, due to Lash's powers.[180] In anger, Johnson attacks her old master and launches him into a concrete wall, engaging in a battle between the two.[184]
    • Leo Fitz tells Phil Coulson that the Containment Module has been breached and Coulson figures that Daisy Johnson managed to escape to confront Hive. Coulson asks Melinda May to take a look, before May orders Fitz to go with her.[184]
    • Holden Radcliffe tells S.H.I.E.L.D. that the Primitives are able to retain some memories of their old lives before they experienced Terrigenesis. Alphonso Mackenzie tells him that the Primitives were former agents of S.H.I.E.L.D., therefore they know the layout of the Playground inside and out. They hear the Primitives entering the vents and growling, forcing the agents to separate and hide.[184]
    • Meanwhile, Leo Fitz and Melinda May enter the holding cell of the Playground, with Fitz asking if Johnson can actually kill Hive. May replies by telling Fitz to fetch some rope if she cannot.[184]
    • As the fight continues, Daisy Johnson whips out a knife and begins stabbing Hive multiple times, commenting that she wants him to suffer. Hive notes that she is the one who is suffering and telling Johnson that he must continue his crusade. Johnson watches as the Hydra QuadCopter carrying the warhead enters the Playground's hangar before Hive knocks her out and places her on the Zephyr One. Hive boards the Zephyr with R. Giyera and Hellfire, who he tells that he will use Johnson as insurance the S.H.I.E.L.D. agents don't try anything foolish and that the Primitives will stay behind to finish the rest of the struggling agents.[184]
    • Meanwhile, in the Playground, Holden Radcliffe follows Phil Coulson and Lincoln Campbell while Elena Rodriguez takes a bullet for Alphonso Mackenzie when the Primitives attack, leaving her severely injured. Radcliffe, Coulson, and Campbell find more Primitives disabling the electricity throughout the Playground.[184]
    • With the memories of Will Daniels and Grant Ward, Hive flies the Zephyr One, ascending the plane to 100,000 feet with the Absolution Virus warhead on board.[184]
    • Running from more Primitives, Alphonso Mackenzie meets up with Phil Coulson, Lincoln Campbell and Holden Radcliffe and take Elena Rodriguez to the workshop of the Playground and hold ground to treat Rodriguez's wounds.[184]
    • Jemma Simmons hides from the Primitives in an empty engine room.[184]
    • As the Zephyr One ascends to 100,000 feet, Hive and R. Giyera explain that once the plane reaches 100,000 feet above the Stratosphere, the Absolution Virus will disperse and spread across the majority of Europe. Before the warhead detentions in the air with Hive's crew inside, they intend to use the S.H.I.E.L.D. Containment Module Daisy Johnson is inside and descended to safety. Unbeknownst to them, Leo Fitz and Melinda May had already infiltrated the aircraft.[184]
    • Giyera sets the time to the detonator of the warhead to 31 minutes.[184]
    • Lincoln Campbell and Alphonso Mackenzie desperately try to heal Elena Rodriguez, but when they start arguing with Holden Radcliffe, Phil Coulson shuts it down and urges them to find something to stop Rodriguez's bleeding. Radcliffe finds a blowtorch and hands it to Campbell, but Rodriguez tells them that she wants Mackenzie to blast her wound with it. Mackenzie fires the blowtorch on her wound, causing Rodriguez to scream.[184]
    • The Primitives bust down the door to the boiler room Jemma Simmons is inside of, huddled close to a furnace and notices that the Primitives right in front of her had gone away because of the heat of the furnace next to her. Simmons realizes the Primitives cannot see under a high temperature and decides to crank up the heat throughout the Playground.[184]
    • Meanwhile, Elena Rodriguez's wound has been sealed and Holden Radcliffe is impressed by Leo Fitz's work with Phil Coulson's Prosthetic Hand.[184]
    • Being held captive, Daisy Johnson sees a Primitive being dragged beneath the floor of the Zephyr One and taken out. She then sees Melinda May and Leo Fitz have infiltrated the plane. May explains that she and Fitz have come to rescue her and stop Hive’s plan. As Fitz goes to open the Containment Module, Johnson tells him to stop and that getting her off would put them at risk.[184]
    • Holden Radcliffe looks at one of the prosthetic eyeballs he used to create, watching it melt and disorient. He realizes that the Primitives must have infrared eyesight, a flaw unintentionally put in place. Radcliffe tests this on an approaching Primitive, but it does not acknowledge Radcliffe’s presence and runs the opposite way. Radcliffe makes his escape and the other S.H.I.E.L.D. agents follow him.[184]
    • After Fitz leaves to go find weapons, May tells Johnson that her powers did not make her powerful or a S.H.I.E.L.D. agent, but that May herself did. Johnson, remembering her losses, tells May that she has nothing left, but May reminds her that Lash saved her life in exchange for his own and tells her that she knows what it is like to want to give up, but the pain will always be there.[184]
    • May is then suddenly knocked unconscious by R. Giyera, who ambushes them and points an MP5 at Leo Fitz. Johnson tries to stall but fails. Fitz tells Giyera that there is a weapon on the plane that is designed to kill him, and if he kills him, then he won’t know what it is. Giyera, still holding Fitz at gunpoint, tells him to find it. Getting down on his knees, Fitz tells him that S.H.I.E.L.D. would never hurt the people under Hive’s sway since they are not in control of their actions. However, Fitz tells Giyera that he was "a murderous swine" before Hive and shoots and kills the inhuman with a Cloaked Gun. Fitz opens Johnson's Containment Module and helps May back on her feet. As the Zephyr One ascends higher, May, Fitz and Johnson are forced to consider their limited options.[184]
    • Phil Coulson, Lincoln Campbell, Alphonso Mackenzie, and Holden Radcliffe, with Elena Rodriguez in tow, make their way to the office of the Playground and reunite with Jemma Simmons, who throws a lamp at Coulson in self-defense. Simmons tells the team that May and Fitz made it onboard Zephyr One and tells them about her solution to the Primitives chasing them regarding the heat. Radcliffe tries to get S.H.I.E.L.D.'s full name correct, but Rodriguez tells him to just say "S.H.I.E.L.D." as she groans in pain. Coulson uses his Prosthetic Hand to call a remote Quinjet to approach the Zephyr and help May, Fitz, and Johnson, personally confronting Hive for enough time to get his friends out. The agents try to object, but Coulson shuts them down, saying he brought Hive to Earth, therefore it is his responsibility to take him out. As the Quinjet approaches and Mackenzie tears down the window of the office, Radcliffe proclaims he likes the way S.H.I.E.L.D. works.[184]
    • As Hive looks at the coordinates on Zephyr One, Hellfire expresses his concerns regarding everyone turning into hideous Primitives, including the women and asks to rework the formula to perfection. Hive ignores him, and instead finds out that R. Giyera has been killed and demands to find the stowaways threatening his plan. Hearing a noise on top of the Zephyr, Hive goes to the docking bay and finds Phil Coulson's hologram projection standing outside of the Quinjet. Hive, seemingly not shocked, asked why he is alone. Coulson says he did not want anyone more people dying for his lapses of judgement. Hive figures out he is hiding something, but after revealing his true face and intending to steal Coulson's real body, Coulson reveals that he is a hologram projection of his body, telling him that he used this distraction to have Alphonso Mackenzie, Lincoln Campbell and Jemma Simmons save Leo Fitz, Melinda May, and Daisy Johnson on board. Finally, Coulson gloats before rephrasing the “Help me, Obi-Wan Kenobi, you’re my only hope” line from Star Wars: Episode IV: A New Hope, infuriating Hive and proceeds to search for the team.[184]
    • Lincoln Campbell is attacked by Hellfire, but defeats him. Hellfire leaves a bomb next to Campbell, badly wounding him. Daisy Johnson reunites with Campbell asks him if she ruined what they had together. Campbell tells her about counseling, but Johnson tells him the pain is not worth remembering and tells him that her destiny is to kill Hive using the Quinjet, as she saw in her vision. Campbell tells her that he knows he went down to face Hive not to kill him, but to be swayed again, and that he understands what it is like to be so addicted to something.[184]
    • The agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. hear the Primitives making their way to them and are on short ideas on how to stop both Hive and the warhead. Coulson and Johnson want to use the Quinjet to possibly send the warhead into space where it can explode safely without harming the Earth. Lincoln Campbell notices that Johnson is wearing the cross necklace kept by Elena Rodriguez and demands where she got it from. Johnson, however, leaves him, going to sacrifice herself to stop Hive and save the world to fullfil her purpose.[184]
    • After Alphonso Mackenzie shows off his new "Shotgun-Ax", they notice Johnson has departed and are ambushed by the Primitives as Hive makes his way to the warhead. A fight ensues between the two groups.[184]
    • Daisy Johnson goes to put the warhead into the Quinjet, attracting Hive's attention. Hive enters Quinjet as Johnson tells him that she intends to fly it away into Outer Space with him inside. However, she and Hive discover Lincoln Campbell had infiltrated the Quinjet and shorted the manual controls so Hive cannot escape. Johnson is pushed away by Campbell, who takes Hive with him on the jet as it launches into the stratosphere, much to Johnson's dismay.
    • Johnson dashes to the communications systems, begging Campbell to pick up the other end of the line. When he answers, Johnson pleads for Campbell to turn around, but Campbell says that this was his destiny and that he stole the cross necklace from her. After the team defeat the Primitives on the Zephyr One, they reunite with a distraught Johnson, who says it was wrong of Campbell to do something so selfish. Campbell chuckles, jokingly telling her with how it felt right saving the world and his lover at the same time. Campbell goes to say "I love you" to Johnson for the first time, but the communications die and cut out as the Quinjet shuts down.[184][93][185]
    • Looking back at Hive, Lincoln Campbell tells him that even if he swayed him, his powers could not turn the Quinjet's power back on or turn the ship around. Hive accepts this as the truth while looking at the warhead's countdown reaching down to 1 minute before detonation—Hive solemnly tells Campbell that together, they will experience death as not friends or enemies, something he is okay with but disappointed.[184]
    • As the Quinjet drifts in space, Campbell gently drifts out of the Quinjet's cockpit towards Hive in the back, feeling somewhat happy that he is experiencing zero-gravity before he dies. Daisy Johnson begs Phil Coulson to bring him back, but says he cannot. Johnson tells Coulson that he was paying for her mistakes, but Coulson states that he was paying for all of their mistakes.[184]
    • Now floating next to each other, Lincoln Campbell and Hive watch as Earth enters the cockpit's window, admiring the planet with Campbell expressing his solemn delight that he got to see the world before he died. Hive murmurs how beautiful and small the Earth was then he had initially imagined and tells Campbell that he only wanted to make it better. Campbell agrees and acknowledges his goal. Hive asks how he could sacrifice himself to save humanity and his S.H.I.E.L.D. friends when they had flaws too great. Campbell replies simply by saying “They're only human”.[184]
    • Lincoln Campbell lets go of the cross necklace and watches it drift in front of him and Hive. Alphonso Mackenzie, Leo Fitz, Jemma Simmons, Melinda May, and Phil Coulson watch from the terminal inside the Zephyr One as the warhead detonation countdown timer reaches 0 and the Quinjet explodes in space: killing both Campbell and Hive while saving the world in the process. Daisy Johnson falls to her knees and bawls her eyes out, devastated by the events accumulated from the effects of Hive's sway and the sacrifice of Campbell. Simmons, tearing up, asks what to do now.[184]
  • Shostakov wakes up on an airplane and sees "Romanoff" and Belova passed out, hearing "Vostokoff" requesting clearance for landing, revealing that the base was in the sky. Shostakov is sedated as the plane touches down.[32]
  • A group of Black Widows trains. "Vostokoff" watches, and the group all stop and look at her. "Vostokoff" walks away and the group continues.[32]
  • Destruction of the Red Room:
    • "Vostokoff" enters Dreykov's office, and Dreykov greets her, asking how it was seeing Shostakov, Romanoff, and Belova. "Vostokoff" says it was awful and confirms for Dreykov that Belova was the only Widow who was cured. Dreykov asks "Vostokoff" to sort the issues with the mind control. "Vostokoff" begins to protest, but Dreykov sits her down and grabs her head, telling "Vostokoff" to cut Belova's brain out and identify the weakness in "her" mind control.[32]
    • Belova is prepared for surgery as a line is drawn on her forehead. Belova says that it is a less cool way to die, and the surgeon activates a surgical tool.[32]
    • Shostakov struggles to break out of his cell while "Romanoff" lays in hers and calls his name.[32]
    • "Vostokoff" asks Dreykov what he will do with "Romanoff." Dreykov describes her as a traitor and tells "Vostokoff" to brainwash her, talking about how powerful it would make him. "Vostokoff" suggests Dreykov speak to Romanoff, but Dreykov reveals that he knows that he already is and takes the Photostatic Veil off of Romanoff's face. Taskmaster pulls a gun on her, but Dreykov tells her not to.[32]
    • Shostakov tells "Romanoff" that he cannot save them and apologizes for his cowardice in refusing to fight for her. "Romanoff" opens the door to his cell and says that she designed the cells, revealing herself to be Vostokoff. Shostakov is upset that he bared his soul to her instead of Romanoff, and Vostokoff contacts Belova over her intercom.[32]
    • Vostokoff tells Belova that she has a knife concealed in her uniform, and Belova reacts, attracting the surgeons' attention. Belova covers for her reaction and Vostokoff tells her where the knife is. Belova uses it to cut her restraints and attacks the surgeon approaching her. She is injected with a sedative but still fights her way through the surgeons. She pulls the needle out of her and Shostakov attempts to use the coms to apologize, until Vostokoff tells him that he does not have an earpiece for him.[32]
    • Vostokoff says that the Red Dust is in cold storage and that Belova needs to expose the Black Widows to it, and Belova sarcastically comments that it will be easy.[32]
    • Dreykov asks Romanoff what his plan is, and Romanoff says that her plan is to kill him. Dreykov points out that he is alive and asks what they do now, and Romanoff asks what her mother's name was. Dreykov tells a long-winded story, just to say that the name on her tombstone was "Unknown."[32]
    • Romanoff says that Dreykov does not feel anything, and asks if he felt something when she killed his daughter. Dreykov realizes that killing his daughter was part of Romanoff's haunted past, causing him to laugh. Dreykov thanks Romanoff and has Taskmaster reveal herself as is his daughter, Antonia Dreykov.[32]
    • Dreykov explains that he put a chip in Antonia's neck and says that he finds her hard to look at. Dreykov says that Antonia is a perfect mimic and that she fights just like the Avengers. Romanoff asks if Antonia can hear her, and Dreykov yells at her for nearly killing her. Dreykov sends Antonia after Vostokoff, Shostakov, and Belova.[32]
    • As Antonia leaves, Romanoff pulls her gun on Dreykov, saying that he sent away the one thing preventing her from killing him. Dreykov suggests that she try and kill him, but Romanoff finds that she cannot. Dreykov taunts her and takes her gun, firing it into the air. Romanoff tries to stab him but stops, and Dreykov takes her knife out of her hands. Romanoff asks how he is controlling her, and Dreykov says that he is not, and rather that there is a pheromonal lock in Romanoff's mind and that she cannot hurt him as long as she can smell him. Dreykov goes to hit Romanoff, making her flinch, but then walks away, saying that he is upset with Vostokoff and will have to kill her.[32]
    • Taskmaster arrives in the basement and sees Shostakov saying that he wants to break something. Vostokoff sees Taskmaster and tells him to fight her. Shostakov enters the computer room and the two begin preparing to fight. Shostakov prepares to say his last words to Vostokoff, but finds that she is already gone.[32]
    • Belova hides in the vent as a group of Red Room soldiers walk in the hallway. She lands in the hallway in a pose, but immediately gets up and finds it weird. Belova incapacitates a guard and uses his hand print to access a room.[32]
    • Vostokoff begins engaging the landing protocol. Dreykov watches Vostokoff on the security camera and deduces that she was planning to land the facility and hand him over to the authorities. He suspends the landing sequence, locking Vostokoff into the computer room.[32]
    • Romanoff asks if Dreykov is planning on brainwashing her, calling the Red Room pathetic and asking when was the last time he had a conversation with someone who was not forced to talk to him. Dreykov says that Romanoff was fighting the wrong war, and that true power comes from undetectable influence. Romanoff says that Dreykov is nothing, and Dreykov begins to talk about the people in his control. Romanoff tells him to stop, angering Dreykov, who yells at her. Romanoff continues taunting Dreykov, prompting him to hit her. Romanoff continues taunting him, and he continues punching her.[32]
    • Romanoff is knocked down, and Dreykov kicks her to the floor and starts saying that he owns the world. Dreykov uses his ring to show Romanoff the locations of the Widows currently deployed. He explains that he gives discarded girls purpose and life.[32]
    • Belova finds the Red Dust and tells Vostokoff, who says that she had a setback. Vostokoff tells Belova to get to the Widows and begins crawling through the vent.[32]
    • Shostakov fights Taskmaster, who knocks him back with her shield. Taskmaster pulls out a knife and they continue fighting. Shostakov lands against the wall and Taskmaster punches him.[32]
    • Dreykov explains that his network of Widows influence global events. Romanoff realizes the full extent of Dreykov's control, and Dreykov says that with her under his control, Dreykov can reveal himself, using the only resource that there are too many of: girls.[32]
    • Romanoff realizes that all of his control comes from his console, and Dreykov confirms. Romanoff smiles, and Dreykov asks why, so Romanoff thanks Dreykov for his cooperation. Romanoff says that he was not strong enough to sever her olfactory nerve, so she slams her nose against the desk, severing it herself. Dreykov presses a panic button, and Romanoff punches him.[32]
    • The Black Widows receive an alert and rush to protect Dreykov.[32]
    • Vostokoff arrives at the engine room and takes down a guard, finding herself surrounded at gunpoint. She holds her hands up and causes an explosion in the room, destroying the engine. She escapes the explosion and tells Belova what happened. Belova finds the Widows' training room empty and straps the vials to a grenade.[32]
    • The Widows approach Dreykov's office.[32]
    • Belova rushes to find them.[32]
    • Taskmaster throws Shostakov through a glass wall, recovers her shield, and begins beating him. Shostakov is thrown back, and Taskmaster prepares to stab him. Vostokoff jumps on top of Taskmaster and throws her into a cell, which Shostakov locks. Taskmaster punches against the wall of the cell and Vostokoff says that they have to go.[32]
    • The engine explodes, causing the facility to shake.[32]
    • Romanoff taunts Dreykov and kicks him. She tells him that he will not break anyone else and prepares to kill him, but a Widow stabs her shoulder and pulls her back. Dreykov recovers and orders the Widows to make Romanoff suffer and kill her, leaving the room. Romanoff says that they do not want to hurt each other, but the Widows attack and Romanoff fights them. Romanoff incapacitates several Widows, but shooting them with her Black Widow's Bite.[32]
    • Helen uses her staff to push Romanoff against a support beam, but Romanoff breaks the staff in two and punches her. Romanoff gets overwhelmed by the Widows, who start kicking and beating on her. A Widow puts Romanoff into a chokehold while others take turns kicking her.[32]
    • Belova appears and explodes the Red Dust over the group, freeing all of the Widows. Belova helps Romanoff to her feet and takes a weapon out of her back. A Widow asks what they should do, and Romanoff tells them to flee and make their own choices.[32]
    • An explosion occurs in the ship and they decide to leave. Romanoff stays behind and says that she will be with her soon.[32]
    • A group of soldiers guard Dreykov as he walks through the facility. Dreykov notices that his ring is missing a tries to go get it, but the ceiling behind him collapses.[32]
    • Romanoff uses the ring to access the monitors and transfer the data to her flash drive. She corrects her nose and waits for the transfer to complete. The facility explodes and the explosions approach Romanoff. The transfer completes and Romanoff gets the flash drive and escapes before the office explodes, jumping out the window.[32]
    • Romanoff grabs the rail of a lower level and watches a group of soldiers on a runway. She lands safely inside the building.[32]
    • A jet takes off as Shostakov and Vostokoff run into another jet. Vostokoff begins preparing to take off and asks after Romanoff and Belova, who Shostakov does not see. The runway falls apart as soldiers approach the jet. The jet falls and Vostokoff navigates it through an explosion. Vostokoff turns around and sees soldiers shooting at her. One lands on the plane, but Shostakov throws his shield at him. The soldier falls back and the shield hits the tail of the plane, causing it to fall. Vostokov struggles to control the plane while Shostakov braces himself.[32]
    • Romanoff runs through the facility as it is destroyed around her, falling to the floor outside Taskmaster's cell. Romanoff sees her and prepares to open the cell, but Taskmaster punches at her. Romanoff pleads with Antonia not to, saying that she will open the door and that she knows that Antonia Dreykov is still in there, refusing to leave her.[32]
    • Romanoff opens the door and Taskmaster walks out. She reaches for Romanoff, but an explosion separates them. Romanoff begins to fall out of the facility, but she manages to hold on by two hooks.[32]
    • Dreykov is brought onto a plane with Belova in pursuit. Romanoff lands on the runway and runs after Belova, who jumps on top of Dreykov's plane. She stands over the engine to the plane as Romanoff catches up to her and prepares her staff. Romanoff pleads with Belova not to sacrifice herself as soldiers aim their guns at her. Belova says that she had fun and shoves her staff into the engine, throwing her backward and causing the plane to explode, killing everyone inside, including Dreykov.[32]
    • Romanoff jumps off the facility after Belova holding a parachute. She falls through the sky and catches up to Belova. She puts a parachute on her back and activates it, allowing them to fall safely. However, Romanoff sees Taskmaster moving toward them and pushes Belova away, sending herself into a freefall.[32]
    • Romanoff and Taskmaster latch on to a piece of debris, and Taskmaster grabs Romanoff. The pair fight as they land on the ground. Taskmaster walks toward Romanoff and they fight. Romanoff steals Taskmaster's sword and points it at Taskmaster. She then puts her hands up and drops the sword, saying that she has had enough. However, Taskmaster grabs Romanoff's throat, giving Romanoff the opportunity to swing around on her arm and jump on her shoulders. She opens Taskmaster's helmet and knocks her to the ground. Taskmaster crawls toward Romanoff, who breaks a vial of Red Dust, freeing her from her father's control.[32]
    • Romanoff and Antonia Dreykov collapse, and Romanoff pulls herself toward Dreykov, apologizing. Dreykov asks if her father is gone, and Romanoff says that he is.[32]
    • Shostakov and Vostokoff wake up from the plane crash, the two embrace, and Vostokoff says that her leg is broken.[177]
    • Romanoff rights herself and watches the facility crash, beginning to call after Belova. She finds her sister and runs over to her, grabbing her head. Belova opens her eyes, sees Romanoff, and says that they are both upside down.[32]
    • Belova rights herself as Romanoff asks for forgiveness for not going back for her. Belova begins to forgive her, and Romanoff says that their family dynamic was real to her as well. Belova hugs Romanoff and thanks her. They are approached by Shostakov and an injured Vostokoff. Romanoff asks Shostakov if he has something to say, and Shostakov says that he would only mess it up. Shostakov takes Romanoff's hand.[32]
    • Thaddeus Ross's army approaches, and Ross is told that they are closing in on Romanoff. Vostokoff asks what the plan is, and Romanoff asks says that Vostokoff, Belova, and Shostakov should go, and that she will stay and fight. The rest of the family insist that they must fight together, but Romanoff insists that they should go, saying that if they can make things work, there may be hope for the Avengers.[32]
    • Belova gives Romanoff her vest, saying that she knows how much Romanoff likes it. Romanoff tells Belova that Vostokoff can copy the formula for the Red Dust so that Belova can free the remaining Widows. A plane lands near them, and the Widows that were freed come out, saying that they would not leave Belova behind. Belova thanks them and walks onto the plane.[32]
    • Vostokoff tells Romanoff to take care of herself, and Romanoff says that she can handle it. Vostokoff says that she knows and walks away. Lerato approaches Dreykov and takes her hand. Vostokoff passes her and says that Dreykov is coming with them. Belova whistles to Romanoff, who whistles in return. The sisters smile at each other before Belova boards the plane with Shostakov and the others, and Romanoff watches it take off.[32]
    • Romanoff turns to face the oncoming vehicles as they turn onto the field and approach her.[32]

29th

  • Rescue of Nakia:
    • Returning home to Wakanda a week after his father's death, T'Challa and Okoye first fly to the Sambisa Forest in Nigeria, hoping to extract Wakandan spy Nakia from her undercover assignment with missing Chibok girls held captive by terrorists.[186][176]
    • Okoye reminds T'Challa not to freeze when he sees Nakia, teasing him about his love for her. He shrugs this off and drops from the jet, throwing EMP Beads, which attach themselves to the terrorists' cars and disable them. T'Challa then hides in a tree as the terrorists get out of their vehicles.[186][176]
    • Leaping from his hiding spot, T'Challa engages the terrorists, the Panther Habit absorbing all their fire. He takes them out with ease, and Nakia steps out to help in the fight. She prevents T'Challa from killing one of the men, who had been forced to join the terrorists against his will. T'Challa loses focus at seeing his ex-girlfriend again, and a terrorist takes advantage of the moment, threatening to shoot one of the girls if T'Challa moves. Okoye, however, takes out the final man, having expected T'Challa to freeze and dropped down herself to help.[186][176]
    • Nakia is frustrated at T'Challa for ruining her assignment, but he informs her of his father's death and the fact that he will be crowned tomorrow, and wanted her to be there. Okoye, meanwhile, frees the Chibok girls.[186][176]
  • As the morning of June 30th dawns in Wakanda, Okoye pilots the trio home. The jet passes through Wakanda's protective dome, and T'Challa returns home to his kingdom.[186][176]
  • The Dora Milaje, an army of women bodyguards who are loyal to the king and led by Okoye, stand to attention at their new king's arrival. T'Challa then reunites with his mother, Ramonda, and teenage sister, Shuri, for the first time since T'Chaka's death. Shuri and Okoye exchange jokes about T'Challa freezing around Nakia, and Shuri then informs T'Challa of an update she has made for the EMP Beads. Ramonda discusses T'Challa's coronation, due to happen later that day, and tells her that T'Chaka is still with them.[186][176]

30th

  • Robbery of the Museum of Great Britain:
    • In London, Erik Stevens, also known as "Killmonger", surveys African artifacts at the Museum of Great Britain. The Museum Director Fiona Thomas speaks to him about each item, informing him of its history. However, when she says that the third item came from Benin, Killmonger corrects her. He tells her that it was stolen by the British in Benin, but originated from Wakanda, and is made of vibranium. She begins to choke, as he tells her that he has had poison put in her drink. Medics seem to arrive on the scene, but suddenly shoot the director and guards, revealing themselves to be in league with Killmonger - one being arms dealer Ulysses Klaue.[186][176]
    • Meanwhile, Killmonger's girlfriend Linda has hacked the security feed to loop footage as if nothing is happening in the African exhibit. Klaue teases a guard with the chance to escape, only to shoot him too, and uses his prosthetic arm to shatter the glass and vibrate the unimportant material off of the vibranium. With the metal acquired, Killonger, Linda, and Klaue escape into an ambulance they have hijacked and make their getaway.[186][176]
  • Coronation of T'Challa:
    • The tribes of Wakanda congregate to celebrate the coronation of T'Challa as their new king. They dance, drum, and chant on boats as they approach Warrior Falls.[186][176]
    • T'Challa arrives at the waterfall in a jet and steps out to face his people. Zuri has T'Challa drink a concoction which strips away the powers of the Heart-Shaped Herb, and each tribe is asked if they wish to challenge him for the throne. While the four tribes do not challenge, the fifth, Jabari Tribe surprises the citizens of Wakanda by making an appearance. Their chief, M'Baku challenges T'Challa.[176]
    • T'Challa and M'Baku engage in a duel for the throne of Wakanda. M'Baku uses his brute strength, whereas T'Challa utilises agility. M'Baku looks set to win as he spears T'Challa in the shoulder, but T'Challa removes the weapon and tackles M'Baku to the ground. Holding him in a lock at the top of the waterfall, T'Challa demands that the Jabari chief yields, not wanting to kill him. M'Baku eventually, reluctantly accepts his defeat.[186][176]
    • Zuri gives T'Challa the necklace of the king, and T'Challa is crowned king of Wakanda. Addressing his subjects, he crosses his arms over his chest and exclaims, "Wakanda forever!", and his people respond following suit.[186][176]
  • A few hours later, as evening arrives in Wakanda, T'Challa is taken to the City of the Dead to commune with his father on the Ancestral Plane. He ingests the Heart-Shaped Herb once more, and Zuri buries him in the soil.[186][176]
  • T'Challa's mind enters the Ancestral Plane and he walks in a savanna. He comes across a tree with several black panthers, and one of the animals leaps from the tree, changing form into T'Chaka. Pleased to see his father again, T'Challa embraces T'Chaka. T'Challa confesses to his father that he does not feel prepared to be king, and T'Chaka advises his son to surround himself with good people. He finishes by telling T'Challa that he is a good man with a good heart, but that because of this, he will face challenges as king.[186][176]
  • T'Challa wakes in the real world, and excitedly tells Zuri of how he had seen his father, having previously not believed the stories.[186][176]
  • After weeks of being unconscious, Matt Murdock slowly wakes. The nuns watching over him asks for his mother to come, calling, "Get Maggie. Tell her he's awake."[187][146][147]
  • Murdock calls for Elektra Natchios, but Sister Maggie Grace says she does not know who that is. Falling out of bed, Grace holds him as he states, disoriented, that he cannot see, just as he did when he first lost his vision.[187][147]
  • Father Paul Lantom visits Murdock in his bed. Murdock asks him about Natchios, confusing Lantom, who points out they buried her months ago. Murdock explains that while it might sound crazy, he was with her, but Lantom says that only he was found.[187][147]

July

1st

  • T'Challa's first day as king of Wakanda begins. He walks among his people, talking to Nakia as he passes through the market.[186][176]
  • The new king contacts Steve Rogers and Bucky Barnes to let them know Wakanda is ready to bring them in to help Barnes.[188][186][176]
  • T'Challa visits his good friend W'Kabi at the rhino paddock, and T'Challa mentions what Nakia has been talking to him about - the prospect of opening up the borders of Wakanda to immigrants. W'Kabi is not happy with this idea, believing T'Challa should protect Wakandans first. Their conversation is interrupted when Okoye, who is also W'Kabi's lover, contacts both of them on their Kimoyo Beads, asking them to come to the throne room.[186][176]
  • In the throne room, Okoye delivers the news that Ulysses Klaue has shown up on their radar again, after evading Wakanda's searches for almost 30 years since he attacked the country and stole vibranium. She tells them that he stole a vibranium weapon from the Museum of Great Britain the day before, and is due to be in Busan, South Korea tomorrow, where a deal is happening. W'Kabi shows particular interest in taking down Klaue, since the arms dealer killed his parents during his attack on the country, but T'Challa tells him he has to remain to protect the Wakandan border. He agrees to go to South Korea, and decides to bring Okoye and Nakia.[186][176]
  • T'Challa visits his younger sister Shuri's lab, where she has new inventions to show him. She demonstrates silent vibranium boots nicknamed "sneakers" and a new version of the Panther Habit which uses nanotechnology to fit within a necklace, as well as absorbing kinetic energy attacks to be redistributed in pulses of energy.[186][176]

2nd

  • The Wakandan Department of Defense sends a message to Shuri warning her not to use her inventions in the world. They worry about possible exposure.[125]
  • Arrest of Ulysses Klaue:
    • The trio of Wakandans arrive at the casino in Busan, South Korea to prepare for Ulysses Klaue, who plans to make a deal to sell vibranium in exchange for diamonds. Princess Shuri remains ready in Wakanda to prove remote backup. Nakia uses one of her spy identities as a Kenyan and talks her way into the casino.[186][176]
    • T'Challa's group enters, and T'Challa is surprised to discovers that the buyer is the CIA, led by Everett Ross. All sides remain tense but no one takes action as Klaue enters with an entourage and goes to Ross.[186][176]
    • As the Wakandan trio debate whether to act, Okoye snaps at Nakia in Xhosa, giving herself away as a Wakandan. One of Klaue's men attacks, and Okoye throws off her wig, abandoning her fake identity and fighting back as a conflict erupts.[186][176]
    • T'Challa confronts Klaue, but the arms dealer uses his weaponized vibranium arm (a special replacement for the arm he lost to Ultron the year before) to cause a distraction and try and escape, with T'Challa's group in pursuit.[186][176]
    • Shuri excitedly takes control of a car and drives, with T'Challa on the roof, in pursuit of Klaue, as Okoye and Nakia drive a vibranium car themselves. Klaue's men fire at the vibranium car to no effect, and shoot at T'Challa, allowing him to absorb the kinetic energy. Okoye throws a vibranium spear to take out one of Klaue's cars, and T'Challa unleashes a blast of kinetic energy to take down Klaue himself.[186][176]
    • T'Challa extends his claws to kill Ulysses Klaue and walks up to him to take him out. However, as Nakia and Okoye arrive on the scene with Everett Ross, T'Challa is reminded not to kill with the whole world watching, as citizens have gathered around with cell phones to record. He takes a moment and steps back, allowing Ross to take Klaue into CIA custody.[186][176]
  • Morning comes in South Korea, and Ulysses Klaue is held for interrogation by the CIA in the CIA South Korean Black Site. T'Challa and Okoye tell Everett Ross that they will take him back to Wakanda, but Ross refuses, agreeing instead to simply let them also question Klaue. Before Ross enters, T'Challa places his hand on his shoulder and thanks him, subtly placing a listening device on Ross' shoulder. Ross interrogates the arms dealer, who claims that his "supplier" is the Wakandans, with his arm cannon being made from their vibranium. He asks what Ross actually knows about the country, and Ross says that he knows it is a third world country of shepherds and textiles, but Klaue informs him this is all a front, and he only stole a tiny amount of the precious metal in comparison to the mountain the Wakandans have.[186][176]
  • Nakia notices a van outside that she considers suspicious. Meanwhile, Ross confronts T'Challa about Klaue's claims, but T'Challa maintains that their country is not particularly special, and that Klaue is simply lying.[186][176]
  • Nakia goes to check the security footage and spots that it has been looped. Realizing something is wrong, she rushes to inform T'Challa and Okoye. Outside, Killmonger, Linda, and a man they have hired get out of the van and set explosives to detonate on the side of the black site building. Nakia gets to her friends, but before she can warn them, the explosions go off and Killmonger breaks into the interrogation room.[186][176]
  • Liberation of Ulysses Klaue: Killmonger shoots at the CIA and Wakandans while Linda and the man they have hired carry Klaue into the back of the van. One of the bullets is aimed at Nakia, but Ross jumps in the way to stop it killing her, hitting him instead. Killmonger then throws a grenade to keep the group from chasing after him, but T'Challa, activating the Panther Habit, leaps onto it to absorb the energy of the explosion. He then pursues Killmonger as their assailant jumps onto the leaving van to escape. However, as he runs to catch the man, Killmonger shoots at him again, causing the kinetic energy build-up in the Panther Habit to overload, going off in a burst of kinetic energy that stops the Black Panther in his tracks. As the attackers get away with Klaue, T'Challa notices a Wakandan royal ring around the main assailant's neck.[186][176]
  • Okoye catches up with T'Challa and ushers him inside to check on Nakia. They find her safe and well, but standing over Ross, who has been severely injured. T'Challa requests that they be allowed to take Ross back to Wakanda, knowing that his only hope of survival and recovery is Shuri. The CIA agree and he stabilizes Ross with a Kimoyo Bead, then they carry him to their ship.[186][176]
  • A few hours later, the trio arrive back at Wakanda with Everett Ross unconscious aboard their ship. Okoye questions whether it is justifiable to bring a foreign intelligence operative back to their country, but Nakia points out that Ross saved her life, and T'Challa decides that despite his duties, they cannot simply let Ross die.[186][176]

3rd

  • The group land and take Ross to Shuri's lab, where Shuri expresses her excitement at fixing another "broken white boy", after starting the project to fix Bucky Barnes' mental conditioning. She analyzes Ross' spine and concludes that she can heal him.[188][186][176]
  • W'Kabi visits T'Challa to ask where they have Ulysses Klaue, but the king sadly admits to his friend that Klaue slipped through their hands. W'Kabi expresses his disappointment to his friend, highlighting that in the almost 3 decades that T'Chaka was king, he had never managed to catch the arms dealer who had killed his parents, and while he had hoped T'Challa would be more successful, he is simply showing himself as no better than his father.[186][176]
  • With Luke Cage's permission, Willis Stryker is transferred to the Raft.[189][190]
  • Assassination of Ulysses Klaue:
    • Arriving at a junkyard where their getaway plane is waiting, Klaue reassures Killmonger that his payment will come shortly. Killmonger waves this away, saying he is not concerned with money, but only hopes that on Klaue's return flight to Johannesburg, he drop them off in Wakanda. The arms dealer refuses, saying they would be crazy to go there, and Killmonger becomes angry, killing the man he and Linda hired and turning his gun on Klaue.[186][176]
    • Klaue grabs Linda and holds a gun to her head, threatening that if Killmonger shoots, he will kill her. Unwavering in his determination, Killmonger unsympathetically kills Linda to remove Klaue's leverage, then pursues him across the junkyard. He eventually catches up to Klaue, shooting him. The man falls to the ground and as Killmonger approaches, tells him that the Wakandans are savages who will treat him as an outsider. However, Killmonger reveals his War Dogs Tattoo inside his lower lip, and Klaue comes to an understanding of what his compatriot's campaign has been about all along. He laughs at his own folly until Killmonger shoots him again, killing him.[186][176]
  • King T'Challa visits Zuri in the City of the Dead and asks him what happened to N'Jobu, believing that the man he saw hours ago must be related to N'Jobu, since his ring was identical to T'Challa's - a ring passed down by T'Chaka's father, Azzuri. Zuri is reluctant to reveal what happened in 1992, having promised T'Chaka to keep it secret, but T'Challa demands the truth as the new king. Zuri sadly confesses what happened, explaining how N'Jobu pulled a gun on him, and T'Chaka reacted by turning and attacking his brother to save Zuri, unintentionally stabbing him in the chest with the Panther Habit claws. Zuri is ashamed as he then tells T'Challa that he and T'Chaka made the decision to leave N'Jobu's son behind, determining him as a risk to their ability to maintain the lie of what happened to N'Jobu, which they believed was important to keep for the good of the country.[186][176]
  • As morning arrives in Wakanda, Killmonger lands his plane at the border of the country and walks to meet with the Border Tribe, carrying a body bag behind him. W'Kabi goes to speak with him and asks what the bag is for. Killmonger claims it is just a "gift", and W'Kabi looks down to see the body of his parents' killer, Ulysses Klaue. Pleased but stunned, he asks the apparent foreigner who he is.[186][176]
  • Everett Ross wakes a little over 24 hours after receiving his bullet wound. Remembering what happened, he reaches for his back, but finds no injury. He confusedly gets up, not understanding where he is or what is happening, and goes over to the only person in sight: Shuri. Shuri is startled by him, but answers his questions, explaining that he is indeed in Wakanda, and that their advanced technology has allowed her to do what he previously thought impossible: heal a bullet wound in just one day. He learns that T'Challa was in fact hiding the truth from him, as Wakanda is overflowing with vibranium resources, with Shuri excitedly showing him inventions such as the magnetic levitation train and sonic stabilizers which temporarily deactivate vibranium and allow it to be transported. She then receives a message from Okoye via her Kimoyo Beads, informing her that a stranger has shown up at the border claiming to have killed Ulysses Klaue. Okoye says that he is also not an outsider, but a Wakandan, showing an image of Killmonger. Ross, however, recognizes him and says that he cannot be Wakandan, as he works for the CIA.[186][176]
  • Natasha Romanoff calls Rick Mason and asks for supplies to help her break Sam Wilson, Clint Barton, and Wanda Maximoff out of prison.[32][191]

4th

  • T'Challa sits with Nakia over a valley in Wakanda, and tells her about his father's actions, trying to understand how the man he loved, respected, and looked up to could have acted this way. Nakia reassures him that despite his father's actions, he need not be defined by them - he gets to decide what kind of king he himself is going to be. T'Challa's Kimoyo Beads suddenly receive a message from Shuri, alerting him that they need him to return to the palace immediately.[186][176]
  • T'Challa and Nakia get to Shuri's lab and Everett Ross tells them about the man who has arrived in Wakanda, Erik Stevens, also known as "Killmonger", and his history in the United States Navy SEALs, his numerous kills fighting in Afghanistan, and time in a JSOC ghost unit. Shuri informs her brother of Stevens' War Dogs Tattoo, but that they have no record of him, and T'Challa silently works out the man is N'Jobu's son.[186][176]
  • Killmonger meets with the Tribal Council to announce his intentions. He declares that he wants the throne, and for Wakanda to arm the 2 billion African diaspora around the world with vibranium so they can fight for themselves. T'Challa claims that he is only king of Wakanda and needs to focus on his people, not the people around the world, and quietly tells Killmonger that the only reason he does not have him killed is because he is aware of who he is. When the king then requests that he be taken away, Killmonger then coaxes the Tribal council into asking who he is, and when the River Tribe Elder gives in, he announces his true identity as N'Jadaka, son of N'Jobu. Ramonda questions his truthfulness, but W'Kabi steps forward and presents Killmonger's royal ring, verifying his story. He challenges T'Challa for the throne, and T'Challa decides he must accept.[186][176]
  • Coronation of Erik Killmonger:
    • Atop Warrior Falls, Zuri gives T'Challa the herb to strip away the powers of the Black Panther ahead of the challenge. Killmonger taunts his cousin, telling him he has killed a multitude of people in the United States, Afghanistan, Iraq, and even the continent of Africa just to get to this moment: to earn the opportunity to kill T'Challa.[186][176]
    • The challenge begins, with T'Challa using a sword and shield and Killmonger wielding a sword and spear. The two are approximately evenly matched, but T'Challa manages to beat his cousin down, holding his sword over him and requesting that he yield.[186][176]
    • Killmonger refuses to give in and gets back on his feet immediately. The duel continues, and T'Challa manages to slash Killmonger's face. However, he becomes only more aggressive in retaliation, fighting back and managing to kick T'Challa down. While the king manages to stand up and resume fighting, Killmonger takes the advantage opportunity, slashing his foe's leg and then his midriff. Finally, he gets in close to T'Challa and uses the spear to stab him in the gut.[186][176]
    • Killmonger goes in to kill the king, saying he is avenging his father, when Zuri suddenly steps in to block him. He tells the challenger that he is to blame for N'Jobu's death, not T'Challa, and that if Killmonger is going to kill someone, it should be him. However, Killmonger simply decides to kill both men and spears Zuri in the stomach.[186][176]
    • T'Challa cries out at his mentor's murder and crawls to him as he dies, but Killmonger calls out to the witnesses, asking if this defeated and helpless man is really fit to be king, and then picks him up from the ground. He lifts the king onto his shoulders to carry him and walks over to the edge of the waterfall, declaring his victory, then throws his foe over the side to fall to his death.[186][176]
    • Shuri and Ramonda are distraught by T'Challa's apparent death, and Nakia ushers them away to safety before Killmonger can take any further action. Killmonger is given the necklace of the king, crowning him as Wakanda's new leader, and the shocked attendees cross their arms in a show of obedience.[186][176]
  • A Jabari fisherman at the bottom of the waterfall is collecting food for the tribe, when he comes across T'Challa, barely alive. He picks him up and takes him to the mountains, and on arrival, M'Baku buries him in snow to keep him comatose, but sustained and alive.[186][176]
  • Nakia goes to see Okoye for help in the fight against Killmonger. However, Okoye refuses, to Nakia's disbelief.
